storage.title: Storage
storage.usedHint: Every binary on this instance, including those no longer in a catalog until garbage collection runs.

kinds.mirrorHint: Pull-through cache of an upstream registry
kinds.alloyHint: One URL that aggregates other repositories

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.emptyBody: Use the tree on the left. Repositories are grouped by ecosystem (Cargo, npm…) and by type: Forge (you publish), Mirror (upstream cache), or Alloy (one URL for several repos).
repositories.noneYet: No repositories yet. Create one to get started.
repositories.createHint: A Forge is hosted storage you publish to. A Mirror caches an upstream (crates.io, npmjs, PyPI, Docker Hub, or OCI charts). An Alloy exposes several Forges and/or Mirrors of the same ecosystem on one URL.
repositories.name: Name
repositories.nameChars: Only letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) are allowed.
repositories.mirrorEcosystems: Mirrors are available for Cargo, npm, PyPI, OCI, Helm, Conan, Maven, NuGet, and Go.
repositories.upstreamInvalid: The upstream URL is not valid.
repositories.alloyNeedsMember: An Alloy needs at least one Forge or Mirror.
repositories.editMembersHint: Change which Forges and Mirrors this Alloy aggregates, and in which order reads resolve.
repositories.missing: That repository does not exist or you do not have access.
repositories.deleteBody: This removes the repository, its artifacts, the package index, and stored objects. This cannot be undone.
repositories.alloyMembers: Aggregates {{members}}. Reads resolve in that order; publish to a member Forge.
repositories.groupedHint: Grouped by name, with each version underneath.
repositories.prefetchHint: Pull a package from the upstream into this Mirror now, without waiting for a client.
repositories.prefetchVersionHint: Optional for Cargo, npm, PyPI, Maven, NuGet, and Go (index only). Required for OCI/Helm (tag or digest) and for Conan (recipe version, e.g. 1.3.1). Conan caches the recipe, not every binary.
repositories.scheduleHint: Re-index packages already cached from the upstream on this interval. The first run is immediate.
repositories.scheduleHoursHint: 1–168 hours. Leave empty or 0 to turn it off.
repositories.scheduleFailed: Could not save the refresh interval
repositories.upstreamAuthHint: Sent only when this Mirror calls its upstream. An empty username sends the secret as a bearer token. A username sends HTTP Basic. The secret is never shown again.
repositories.upstreamAuthRemoveHint: Later prefetch and pull-through calls go out without an Authorization header.
repositories.membersEmpty: There are no Forge or Mirror repositories for this ecosystem. Create one first so you can add it.
repositories.membersHint: Selection order is resolution order: the first member wins if the same version exists in more than one.

upstream.npmHint: Base URL of the npm registry (for example https://registry.npmjs.org/).
upstream.ociHint: OCI registry URL (for example https://registry-1.docker.io). Official Docker Hub images resolve as library/<name>.
upstream.helmHint: OCI chart registry URL (for example https://registry-1.docker.io). Use the full name, such as bitnami/nginx.
upstream.conanHint: Conan Center URL (for example https://center2.conan.io). Older remotes use https://center.conan.io.
upstream.cargoHint: Sparse index base URL (without the sparse+ prefix).
upstream.nugetHint: NuGet V3 service index URL (for example https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json).

password.policy: At least 8 characters, with one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, and one digit.
password.mismatch: The new password and confirmation do not match

settings.title: Settings
settings.accountHint: Current session identity and password change.
settings.forgotAdmin: If you forgot your password, ask an administrator to reset it. No recovery emails are sent.
settings.instanceHint: Public URL that Cargo and other clients should use. Taken from PUBLIC_BASE_URL.
settings.ssoOff: Not configured. Set OIDC_ISSUER and OIDC_CLIENT_ID to enable it.
settings.groupsHint: The groups you belong to decide which repositories you see.
settings.noGroupsAdmin: You are not in any group. As Admin you see every repository.
settings.noGroupsUser: You are not in any group. You see unrestricted repositories according to your instance role.
settings.groupNoRepos: This group has no repositories assigned yet.

notFound.default: The page you are looking for does not exist.

search.title: Search
search.description: Find packages already indexed in Forge and Mirror repositories without walking the tree. A Mirror only shows what someone has resolved or cached; it does not query upstream.
search.emptyBody: For example serde, lodash, or alpine. Internal layers and Alloy aggregates are not listed.
search.noHitsHint: Try another name, or publish / resolve the package in a Forge or Mirror.

assays.title: Assays
assays.description: Instance assays: composition, declared licenses, and impurities of each published or cached version. They include lockfiles, distro packages, and images declared in Helm. They run automatically on publish or cache; they do not block install or publish.
assays.emptyBody: Publish a package or install/pull against a Mirror: the assay starts on its own. You can also open a version and press Assay. The inventory is queried against OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities). Helm and Conan show composition when Chart.yaml or requires is present; OSV does not index them.
assays.dialogHint: Metallurgical assay of the artifact: composition (inventory, declared licenses) and impurities (known vulnerabilities from OSV). It does not block downloads or publishes.
assays.noVulns: No known vulnerabilities for the concrete versions in this inventory.

security.title: Security
security.description: Issue and revoke API tokens for the UI, cargo publish, and automations.
security.emptyBody: Create one to authenticate cargo publish or integrations.
security.expiresHint: Optional. Leave empty for a token that does not expire.
security.scopeHint: Leave both unchecked for full access, same as a login session.
security.repositoryHint: Leave every box unchecked to allow every repository you can access, including ones created later. Check repositories to limit the token to those.
security.repositoryEmpty: No repositories yet. An empty selection still covers repositories created later.
security.copyNowHint: This secret is shown only once. In ~/.cargo/credentials.toml use [registries.ferrobox] and token = "fb_…".

users.title: Users
users.description: Create accounts, assign roles, and reset passwords. If someone forgets theirs, an administrator resets it here.
users.newHint: Username and email must be unique. The password must meet the instance policy.
users.newRobotHint: A CI account: no password and no SSO. You get one API token now; copy it immediately.
users.robotTokenHint: This is the only time the robot token is shown. Use it in CI as a Bearer token.
users.deleteTokens: API tokens for this user will be revoked. This cannot be undone.
users.resetHint: Assign a new password to “{{name}}”. You cannot reset your own here: use Settings.
users.mismatch: The password and confirmation do not match

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Open a group to see members and repositories. Editing changes who belongs and what they can access. A group member only sees those repositories. Anyone in no group still follows the instance role on unrestricted repositories.
groups.editHint: Choose members and repositories. People in this group only see those repositories, as Reader or Developer.
groups.viewHint: Members and repositories of this group. Members only see those repositories.
groups.noneYet: No groups yet. Create one to restrict access to specific repositories.
groups.deleteBody: Members and repository access for this group will be removed. Repositories themselves are not deleted.
groups.newHint: Groups collect users and limit which repositories they can see. Anyone in a group only sees the repositories assigned to their groups.
groups.nameHint: Letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores. Maximum 64 characters.
groups.membersHint: Users who belong to this group.
groups.membersEditHint: Checked users belong to this group.
groups.noUsers: There are no users on the instance.
groups.reposHint: Repositories this group can see, with the granted role.
groups.reposEditHint: Assign a role per repository. “No access” leaves that repository out of the group.
groups.noReposAssigned: This group has no repositories assigned.

artifacts.emptyForgeCargo: Publish a crate with cargo publish --registry ferrobox, or upload a generic binary.
artifacts.refreshHint: Reload packages published outside this page
artifacts.cosignTitle: The Cosign signature verifies against this repository’s public keys
artifacts.signedTitle: There is a Cosign or Notation signature linked to this tag
artifacts.unyankHint: Offer this version again in new resolutions
artifacts.yankHint: Stop using it in new resolutions; it stays downloadable if already pinned
artifacts.deleteObject: The stored object, metadata, and index entry will be removed. This cannot be undone.
artifacts.deleteFile: This file will be removed from storage. The rest of the version is unchanged. This cannot be undone.

admission.title: Policies
admission.description: On install, pull, or promote into this Forge: deny or only warn if the artifact is unsigned, has a finding at or above a severity, or declares a denied license. Signature applies to OCI/Helm. License uses the last ready assay. A known-vulnerability rule denies the pull when the vulnerability feed is missing or that assay is not ready. A Mirror uses this rule; an Alloy uses each member. Dry run ignores whether the rule is enabled.
admission.enableHint: If unchecked, the rule is saved but does not block or warn on pull or promote.
admission.whenPull: When installing, pulling, or promoting in
admission.profileOpenchainHint: Finding ≥ Medium, warn. Helps operate an OpenChain security program; it is not certification.
admission.profileCopyleftHint: Deny GPL / AGPL / SSPL. A common inbound policy; ISO 5230 does not require it.
admission.findingHint: Uses the last ready assay. If this is not Off, a missing vulnerability feed or an assay that is not ready denies the pull.
admission.licensesHint: SPDX ids, one per line. Exact match, case-insensitive. Empty = off.
admission.savedOn: Policy saved. Later pulls will be evaluated.
admission.keysHint: The ones from cosign generate-key-pair. Several, one after another. Empty: “not verified” lets no image through.
admission.noKeysBody: With “not verified” and an empty PEM, no image counts as verified. Paste at least one public key before enabling the rule.
admission.step2Hint: Walks the inventory as if the rule were enabled. It does not block pulls.
admission.step3Hint: Save applies the rule to later pulls. Dry-run first to see which packages would be left out.
admission.readOnly: Read only: a Developer or Admin can dry-run and save.
admission.eventsHint: Latest pulls that triggered the active rule. Warn lets them through and logs them here.
admission.savedUnsigned: Policy saved. Pulls of unverified images will be evaluated from now on.
admission.savedUnsignedSig: Policy saved. Pulls of unsigned images will be evaluated from now on.
admission.savedOff: Policy saved. It is disabled: pulls are not blocked.
admission.noneWouldFire: No package would trigger the rule. {{allowed}}.
admission.loadFailed: Could not load the saved policy
admission.loadFailedHint: {{message}}. You can still configure and dry-run; save needs the policy table.
admission.migrationHint: Then restart the backend. Dry run works without migrating; save does not.

retention.saved: Policy saved. Nothing was removed from the catalog; press Dry run to see the effect.
retention.applyHint: The policy will be saved and versions outside it will leave the catalog. Disk is not freed until garbage collection. On a Mirror, the next install may cache them again. This cannot be undone.
retention.limitsInvalid: Limits must be whole numbers, or left empty
retention.title: Retention
retention.description: Keep the N most recent versions and/or those published in the last N days. Empty = no limit. Apply removes them from the catalog; install and publish are not blocked. Disk is freed in Settings → Garbage collection.
retention.applyWithPreview: {{preview}} The policy will be saved and that list will leave the catalog. Disk is not freed until garbage collection. On a Mirror, the next install may cache them again. This cannot be undone.
retention.step2Hint: Uses the numbers in the form; you do not need to save. Nothing leaves the catalog.
retention.readOnly: Read only: a Developer or Admin can dry-run and apply.
retention.step3Hint: Apply saves these numbers and drops from the catalog what Dry run showed. Dry-run first. Save does not touch the catalog. Disk is freed later, in Settings.
retention.loadFailed: Could not load the saved policy
retention.loadFailedHint: {{message}}. You can still configure and dry-run; save and apply need the policy table.
retention.migrationBody: The policy table does not exist. From the backend/ directory run:
retention.migrationHint: Then restart the backend. Dry run works without migrating; save and apply do not.

quota.title: Quota
quota.description: Disk cap for this repository. Empty = no limit. It counts every binary, including those no longer in the catalog until garbage collection runs. A publish that does not fit is rejected.
quota.limitPositive: The cap must be a number greater than 0, or left empty
quota.limitRange: The cap must be between 1 byte and 10 TiB
quota.unlimitedSaved: Unlimited quota. Later publishes are not rejected for size.
quota.limitSaved: Cap saved. A publish that does not fit will return a conflict.
quota.overLimit: Usage is over the cap. Later publishes will fail until you raise the limit or free disk in Settings → Garbage collection.
quota.emptyHint: Leave the amount empty to remove the cap. 1 GiB = 1024 MiB.
quota.readOnly: Read only: a Developer or Admin can change the cap.
quota.migrationBody: The quota table does not exist. From the backend/ directory run:
quota.migrationHint: Then restart the backend. Usage works without migrating; save does not.

worm.title: WORM
worm.description: Write-once lock for this repository. When enabled, delete, yank, unyank, retention apply, and per-repository garbage collection return 403. Publish is unchanged.
worm.saveFailed: Could not save the WORM lock
worm.loadFailed: Could not load the WORM lock
worm.enableHint: Blocks deleting artifacts or the repository, yank and unyank, applying retention, and collecting garbage for this repository.
worm.enabledSaved: WORM enabled. Delete, yank, retention apply, and per-repository GC are blocked.
worm.disabledSaved: WORM disabled. Delete, yank, and retention apply are allowed again.
worm.readOnly: Read only: a Developer or Admin can change the lock.
worm.migrationBody: The WORM table does not exist. From the backend/ directory run:
worm.migrationHint: Then restart the backend. The lock reads as off without migrating; save does not.

gc.title: Garbage collection
gc.description: Deletes binaries from disk that are no longer in any catalog (versions dropped by retention, leftovers from Delete, OCI layers without a manifest). Dry run does not change anything. Install and publish stay available while it runs.
gc.applyHint: Orphan binaries across the instance will be deleted from disk. Dry-run first to see the list. This cannot be undone.
gc.readOnly: Only a Developer or Admin can dry-run and collect.
gc.previewEmpty: Nothing to drop from the catalog with this policy.
gc.previewDrop: {{count}} versions would leave the catalog. Disk is not freed until garbage collection.
gc.appliedDrop: Dropped {{count}} versions from the catalog. Disk space is freed in Settings → Garbage collection.
gc.previewOrphansEmpty: There are no orphan binaries to delete.

permissions.title: Permissions by role
permissions.description: Roles apply to the whole instance. A Reader reads; a Developer also publishes and manages repositories; an Admin also manages accounts and groups. A group member only sees repositories assigned to their groups. Anyone in no group sees unrestricted repositories, according to their instance role.
permissions.tokens: Manage own API tokens and change own password
permissions.configure: Configure retention, quota, WORM, and HTTP notifications
permissions.users: Create users, change roles, and delete accounts

feed.title: Vulnerability feed
feed.empty: No vulnerability feed has been imported.
feed.pageDescription: One index for every repository. Assays use it when it is loaded, and api.osv.dev otherwise.
feed.loadFailed: Could not load the vulnerability feed
feed.instance: One index for the whole instance. Deleting a repository leaves it in place.
feed.hint: A rejected signature does not replace the active index. Sync now checks the saved reference.
feed.saveFailed: Could not save the sync settings
feed.syncRejected: The pull was rejected and the active index was kept
feed.syncFailed: Could not sync the vulnerability index
feed.removeFailed: Could not remove the vulnerability feed
feed.removeDescription: This deletes the index and the saved sync settings for the whole instance. Assays run again without this index. Deleting a repository does not do this.

audit.title: Audit
audit.description: Who published, yanked, changed a group, or created a user. The last 200 writes on the instance.

replica.title: Instance replica
replica.description: Push this catalog to a Forge on another FerroBox, or pull a remote Forge into this one. The remote repository must already exist and use the same ecosystem. An optional interval runs that push or pull in the background.
replica.loadFailed: Could not load the replica target
replica.directionHint: Push sends this catalog to the remote Forge. Pull downloads the remote Forge into this repository.
replica.remoteUrlHintPush: Backend origin of the destination instance, for example http://127.0.0.1:3001. Use the FerroBox port, not the Vite port.
replica.remoteUrlHintPull: Backend origin of the source instance, for example http://127.0.0.1:3000. Use the FerroBox port, not the Vite port.
replica.destinationHint: Forge on the remote instance. Same ecosystem. Import still rejects a Mirror or an Alloy.
replica.destinationHintPull: Forge on the remote instance to pull from. Same ecosystem.
replica.tokenPlaceholder: Token with write access on the destination
replica.tokenPlaceholderPull: Token with read access on the source
replica.tokenKept: Token is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
replica.tokenHint: A robot or user token from the destination instance. It is not shown again.
replica.tokenHintPull: A robot or user token from the source instance. It is not shown again.
replica.intervalHint: 1–10080 minutes (up to one week). Empty or 0 disables the cron. A policy that has never run is due on the next tick (~30s).
replica.saveFailed: Could not save the replica target
replica.pushed: Pushed {{packages}} packages and {{artifacts}} artifacts ({{skipped}} already there).
replica.pulled: Pulled {{packages}} packages and {{artifacts}} artifacts ({{skipped}} already there).
replica.readOnly: You can see the target. Changing it needs write access.

registry.publicUrlFailed: Could not load the instance public URL.
registry.cargoFailed: Could not load the Cargo registry configuration.
registry.oci: This repository implements Distribution Spec v2: docker push and docker pull work natively.
registry.ociStep1Hint: On local HTTP, Docker requires insecure-registries: ["{{host}}"] in /etc/docker/daemon.json and a daemon restart. Copy the full UUID (8-4-4-4-12). If an old login is not enough for push, run docker logout {{host}} and sign in again.
registry.ociStepPushHint: The image name is <UUID>/demo (a slash also works, e.g. bitnami/nginx). The registry is the host root (/v2/), not an extra prefix.
registry.ociMirrorHub: With Docker Hub as upstream, alpine:latest resolves as library/alpine.
registry.ociStepVerifyHint: FerroBox exposes the Referrers API and sha256-<digest>.sig tags. Cosign resolves them against the same registry. On local HTTP add --allow-insecure-registry.
registry.ociStepSignHint: The signature is stored as an OCI accessory of the image (.sig tag or Referrers API). The UI shows the Signed badge. On local HTTP add --allow-insecure-registry. This step does not require a signature on docker pull.
registry.ociMirrorBody: This Mirror caches images from upstream (for example Docker Hub) the first time docker pull resolves them. It does not accept docker push or yank.
registry.ociAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates OCI Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. docker pull resolves against members, in order. It does not accept docker push: publish to a member Forge.
registry.conan: This repository implements the Conan v2 API (revisions). conan upload and conan install talk to /conan/<UUID>/.
registry.conanAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates Conan Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. conan install resolves against members, in order. It does not accept conan upload: publish to a member Forge.
registry.conanMirrorBody: Conan only talks to this URL. FerroBox fetches the upstream (Conan Center) on the first miss and caches it. The remote must use this repository UUID — a leftover ferrobox remote from another repo will not see this Mirror. It does not accept conan upload or yank.
registry.conanStep1Hint: Copy the full UUID (8-4-4-4-12). The remote URL is {{url}}. add creates it; update overwrites an existing ferrobox remote so it targets this repository.
registry.conanStep2Hint: Username __token__. When asked for the password, paste the token created in Security.
registry.maven: This repository uses the Maven HTTP layout. Releases and SNAPSHOT versions share one URL. mvn deploy and Gradle publishing talk to /maven/<UUID>/.
registry.mavenMirrorBody: This Mirror caches packages from upstream the first time mvn or Gradle resolves them. It does not accept mvn deploy or yank.
registry.mavenAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates Maven Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. Resolves against members, in order. It does not accept mvn deploy: publish to a member Forge.
registry.mavenStep1Hint: Copy the full UUID (8-4-4-4-12). Releases and SNAPSHOT use this same URL.
registry.mavenStep2Hint: Username __token__. When asked for the password, paste the token created in Security.
registry.mavenStep3: 3. Point pom.xml at this registry and deploy
registry.mavenStep3Hint: distributionManagement.repository and snapshotRepository use the same URL.
registry.nuget: This repository implements the NuGet V3 API. dotnet nuget push and dotnet restore talk to /nuget/<UUID>/v3/.
registry.nugetMirrorBody: This Mirror caches packages from upstream the first time dotnet restore resolves them. It does not accept dotnet nuget push or unlist.
registry.nugetAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates NuGet Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. Resolves against members, in order. It does not accept dotnet nuget push: publish to a member Forge.
registry.nugetStep1Hint: Copy the full UUID (8-4-4-4-12). This is the source you pass to dotnet nuget add source.
registry.nugetStep2: 2. Add the source with an API token
registry.nugetStep2Hint: Username __token__. When asked for the password or --api-key, paste the token created in Security.
registry.nugetStep3Hint: Versions are immutable. Unlist a version to hide it from search; it stays downloadable if already pinned.
registry.go: This repository implements the GOPROXY protocol. go get and go mod download talk to /go/<UUID>/.
registry.goMirrorBody: This Mirror caches modules from upstream the first time go get resolves them. It does not accept uploads or yank.
registry.goAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates Go Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. Resolves against members, in order. It does not accept uploads: publish to a member Forge.
registry.goStep1Hint: Copy the full UUID (8-4-4-4-12). This is the value of GOPROXY.
registry.goStepEnv: 2. Point the go command at this proxy
registry.goStep2Hint: The zip must contain module@version/go.mod. The token is created in Security.
registry.npm: This repository implements the npm registry protocol: npm publish and npm install work natively.
registry.npmMirrorBody: This Mirror caches packages from upstream the first time npm install resolves or downloads them. It does not accept npm publish or yank.
registry.npmAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates npm Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. npm install resolves against members, in order. It does not accept npm publish: publish to a member Forge.
registry.pypi: This repository implements the PyPI protocol: twine upload and pip install work natively.
registry.pypiMirrorBody: This Mirror caches packages from upstream the first time pip install resolves or downloads them. It does not accept twine upload or yank.
registry.pypiAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates PyPI Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. pip install resolves against members, in order. It does not accept twine upload: publish to a member Forge.
registry.pypiStepInstallHint: The trailing slash on /simple/ is required. On local HTTP, pip uses --trusted-host and uv uses --allow-insecure-host. Both request the PEP 691 JSON index.
registry.pypiStepTwineHint: Put it in ~/.pypirc. The token is created in Security. Copy the full UUID (8-4-4-4-12).
registry.pypiStepInstallOtherHint: On local HTTP, uv uses --allow-insecure-host instead of --trusted-host. pip and uv request the PEP 691 JSON index.
registry.helm: Charts are published as OCI artifacts (Distribution Spec v2). helm push and helm pull talk to /v2/ at the host root.
registry.helmMirrorBody: This Mirror caches OCI charts from upstream the first time helm pull resolves them. It does not accept helm push or yank.
registry.helmAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates Helm Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. helm pull and helm install resolve against members, in order. It does not accept helm push: publish to a member Forge.
registry.helmStep1Hint: Copy the full UUID (8-4-4-4-12). On local HTTP, helm push / helm pull need --plain-http. If a previous push failed with 401, helm logout {{host}} and sign in again: Helm may have cached an anonymous token from the /v2/ ping.
registry.helmStepHint: The chart lives at oci://<host>/<UUID>/<name>. The name comes from Chart.yaml. Names with a slash (for example bitnami/nginx) also work.
registry.cargo: This repository implements Cargo’s sparse index protocol: cargo publish, yank, search, add, and build work natively.
registry.cargoMirrorBody: This Mirror caches packages from upstream the first time they are resolved or downloaded. It does not accept cargo publish or cargo yank.
registry.cargoAlloyBody: This Alloy aggregates Cargo Forges and/or Mirrors on one URL. cargo add and cargo build resolve against members, in order; the first wins if the same version exists. It does not accept cargo publish or cargo yank: publish to a member Forge.
registry.cargoStep1: 1. Register the index in your Cargo configuration
registry.cargoStep1Hint: You can put it in ~/.cargo/config.toml or in the crate’s .cargo/config.toml (for example demo-ferrobox/.cargo/config.toml).
registry.cargoStep2Token: 2. Save an API token (only to publish or yank)
registry.cargoStep2TokenHint: The index and downloads are public: cargo add and cargo build do not need a token. Issue one in Security and store it in ~/.cargo/credentials.toml (Cargo does not read .cargo/credentials.toml in the project). Alternative: cargo login --registry ferrobox or cargo publish --registry ferrobox --token fb_…. Do not commit the token.
registry.cargoAlloyPublishHint: To publish, point cargo publish --registry at a member Forge, not this Alloy.
registry.npmStep1Hint: Put it in the package .npmrc or in ~/.npmrc. The token is created in Security. The trailing slash on the URL is required.

access.title: Access
access.description: If you assign one or more groups, only those groups (and administrators) will see this repository. A group member does not see the other repositories. With no groups, anyone in no group follows the instance role.
access.empty: There are no groups. Create them in Groups to restrict this repository.
access.unrestricted: The repository is visible again according to the instance role

promote.title: Promote to another Forge
promote.hint: Copies {{subject}} to a Forge of the same ecosystem. The destination version is published again; a yank on the source is not inherited. The destination admission policy is evaluated against the source package.

setup.title: Set me up
setup.cargo: Copy these snippets into your crate or ~/.cargo. The token is created in Security.
setup.npm: Copy these snippets into .npmrc. The token is created in Security.
setup.pypi: Copy these snippets into ~/.pypirc or the pip / uv command. The token is created in Security.
setup.oci: Copy these snippets for docker login / docker push and, if you want, cosign sign. The token is created in Security.

webhooks.title: HTTP notifications
webhooks.description: FerroBox sends a JSON POST when an event happens. Publish and install do not wait for the reply: a down destination does not block the catalog.
webhooks.readOnly: Only someone who can write to this repository configures notifications.
webhooks.migrationBody: From the backend/ directory run sqlx migrate run and restart the backend.
webhooks.assayCompletedHint: Includes finding counts (Critical, High, …). Install does not wait.
webhooks.packagePublishedHint: When publishing to a Forge or caching in a Mirror.
webhooks.deleteBody: Notifications will stop going to this URL. Delivery history is also removed.
webhooks.noDeliveries: No deliveries yet. Use Test for a ping.
